cat > /tmp/pr-b.md <<'BODY'
## Summary

When a workspace's inference provider ran dry, its `inference_providers` row kept reading `active` while every Behavior failed. Nothing anywhere wrote provider health, so the only way to find the cause was to group `runs.error_message` by hand — which is how buremba's z.ai balance exhaustion (`429 Insufficient balance or no resource package`) went unnoticed for two days and ~85 failed runs.

Both halves of the signal already pass through `POST /worker/response`, so the writeback lives there and the two cannot drift apart:

- a terminal `PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` / `PROVIDER_AUTH` marks the provider named by `errorContext.provider` as `status = 'error'` carrying the provider's own message (truncated to 500 chars);
- the next completion that provider serves clears it, via a new `providerSlug` the worker stamps on the completion row — the success-side counterpart of `errorContext.provider`, following the existing `repliedInBand` latch pattern.

`errorMessage` and `updatedAt` are added additively to the provider-list response so the settings page can say why and when.

No schema change: `inference_providers.status` (`active|disabled|error`) and `error_message` have existed since the table was created.

Follows #2521 (parking a Behavior when the balance is empty) — that one stops the burn, this one makes the cause visible. Part of #2350; provider **failover** (gap 1) still needs the product decision and is untouched.

### Design properties worth checking

- **Observational, so routing stays fail-open.** Nothing in credential resolution or model routing reads `status` — verified with `git grep status origin/main -- provider-secrets.ts`, every reference is a SELECT for display. A dropped write costs a stale label, never a stranded workspace. That is why `recordProviderHealth` swallows its own errors rather than failing a delivered turn; it is not durable dispatch/delivery state.
- **Awaited, not fire-and-forget.** It returns without touching the DB unless the row is terminal, so the per-delta hot path pays nothing while terminal rows get a deterministic write instead of one racing the response.
- **`disabled` is an operator decision** and is never overwritten in either direction. The clear is predicated on `status = 'error'`, so a healthy turn is an indexed no-op, and traffic can never re-enable what an operator switched off.
- **Tenant safety.** The org comes from the signed worker token, the slug from the body — so the worst a compromised worker can do is mislabel a provider its own organization already owns. Pinned by a test.
- **Only quota/auth mark the row.** `PROVIDER_UNKNOWN_MODEL` / `PROVIDER_BASE_URL_UNRESOLVED` are configuration errors, not provider health, so they deliberately do not.

## Test plan
- [x] `make pre-pr` clean (build + typecheck + knip + lint + exposed-surface naming)
- [x] Tests run: store suite 15/15 (vitest, embedded PG18), gateway handler suite 17/17 (`bun test`, real Hono handler + real DB), agent-worker transport suite 4/4
- [x] Bug fix: mutation evidence pasted below

### Mutation evidence

New capability, so the meaningful proof is that each guard is load-bearing. Four mutations, each verified as actually applied to the source before running:

**A — dropped `AND status <> 'disabled'` from `markInferenceProviderUnhealthy`**
```
A applied: disabled guard removed from mark
   × inference-provider health writeback > never overwrites an operator-disabled provider in either direction 137ms
      Tests  1 failed | 14 passed (15)
```

**B — dropped `AND status = 'error'` from `clearInferenceProviderError`**
```
B applied: error-only guard removed from clear
   × inference-provider health writeback > never overwrites an operator-disabled provider in either direction 124ms
      Tests  1 failed | 14 passed (15)
```

**C — broadened the errorCode allowlist to any code**
```
C applied: errorCode allowlist broadened to any code
(fail) POST /worker/response — inference-provider health > an unrelated failure leaves provider health alone
 16 pass
 1 fail
```

**D — removed the `providerSlug` stamp from `signalCompletion`**
```
(fail) the completion carries the recorded provider slug
(fail) re-resolution within a turn stamps the provider that ran last
 2 pass
 2 fail
```

All four restored, all suites green:
```
 17 pass  0 fail    (gateway handler)
      Tests  15 passed (15)    (store)
 4 pass  0 fail     (agent-worker stamp)
```

## Notes

**Not verified end-to-end against a live provider.** The gateway tests drive the real Hono `/response` handler against a real Postgres and assert the row transitions, and the agent-worker test asserts the slug reaches the completion body — but no test runs a real worker against a real exhausted provider. The seam between `onModelResolved` and the transport latch is covered by typecheck plus the in-process transport test, not by a booted worker. Worth a prod spot-check after rollout: exhaust a provider, confirm the settings row flips to `error`, then confirm a successful turn clears it.
BODY

`advanceScheduleAfterTerminalFailure` (#2335) already killed the tight re-claim loop, and a
later PR added `providerQuotaResetNotBefore` so a 429 naming `reset at <date>` parks until
then. What remained: a 429 that names **no** reset. z.ai's is
`429 Insufficient balance or no resource package` — a BALANCE exhaustion, which never
self-heals on a timer, so it fell through to the plain cron advance and burned one failed
run per tick forever.

## #2521 — reset-less balance park (MERGED `f0443c28`)

`packages/server/src/watchers/schedule-cursor.ts`. Both helpers now fall back to a flat
**24h** park when the message carries balance/billing wording and no date. A provider-named
reset still wins. The three terminal paths (cloud `run-completion.ts`, device
`run-lifecycle.ts`, reply-to-source `chat-response-bridge.ts`) already route through these
two functions, so there were no new call sites.

**The trap that made this non-trivial:** Gemini's per-minute free-tier 429 reuses OpenAI's
billing sentence `exceeded your current quota` VERBATIM. Wording alone cannot tell a
balance from a window. The discriminator is a **provider-named retry horizon** —
`\bretry[-_ ]?(?:in|after|delay)\b` — and any message carrying one is never day-parked.
Caught by `make review-fix`, not by me.

Flat 24h, not escalating backoff: recovery is a human adding funds, which no wait predicts,
and a growing park would need durable per-provider attempt state. Manual triggers still run
immediately (parking only moves the cron cursor; the due predicate excludes
`dispatch_source = 'manual'`).

evidence (it previously also required a parseable date), so a stray `payment required` in
unrelated stderr would day-park a Behavior.

`inference_providers.status` (`active|disabled|error`) and `error_message` have existed
since the table was created — **no migration needed**, check before proposing one.

Both halves of the signal already pass through `POST /worker/response`
(`packages/server/src/gateway/gateway/index.ts` → new `recordProviderHealth`), so the
writeback lives at that one chokepoint:
- terminal `PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` / `PROVIDER_AUTH` + `errorContext.provider` → mark;
- next completion carrying the new `providerSlug` → clear.

`providerSlug` is stamped by the worker on the COMPLETION row only, following the
`repliedInBand` precedent: `HttpWorkerTransport.recordProviderSlug`, called from
`worker.ts`'s `onModelResolved` behind an `instanceof HttpWorkerTransport` narrowing.
**The core `WorkerTransport` interface was NOT widened** — `recordInBandReply` set that
precedent and it is much cheaper.

Key property that makes best-effort safe: **nothing routes on `status`.** Verified with
`git grep status origin/main -- provider-secrets.ts` — every reference is a SELECT for
display. So routing stays fail-open and a dropped write costs a stale label, never a
stranded workspace. That is the justification for swallowing errors; it is NOT a violation
of the fail-closed rule because this is not dispatch/delivery state.

Awaited rather than `void`-called: it returns without touching the DB unless the row is
terminal, so the per-delta hot path pays nothing and terminal rows get a deterministic
write instead of one racing the response (which also removes a test race).

**Gap 1 — provider failover — remains unbuilt and still blocked on the product call**
(whose budget pays for a customer's exhausted quota; whether silently rerouting a
workspace's prompts to another vendor is acceptable). The design sketched in
[[project_behaviors_down_zai_quota]] still stands: write a per-(org, provider) cooldown and
make `providerIsRoutable()` consult it, so the EXISTING pre-dispatch walk fails over for
free. Note this PR's `status` column is deliberately NOT that lever.

  make review` / `make review-fix` WORKS and produced the real bug above. Reverses

  recorded availability window.

  worktree, and `make pre-pr` FAILS on it** — biome checks it even though `.pi/` is in
  `.gitignore`. `rm -rf .pi` before pre-pr. (Unfixed class bug in the gate.)
- Integration suites need `env -u DATABASE_URL PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/node@22/bin:$PATH"`
  to get the embedded PG18 — see [[reference_local_server_integration_tests]].

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Prod smoke: verify the DEPLOYED system, not an artifact.
#
# The other two gates each answer a question this one cannot:
#
#   app-image-smoke        is the image broken?      (boots with its OWN env + db)
#   published-artifact-…   can users install it?     (npm tarball, 4 environments)
#   THIS                   did the rollout land, and does prod work with the
#                          REAL Helm config, ingress, TLS, and database?
#
# Nothing here overlaps. An image smoke can never catch a missing Helm env var,
# a broken ingress route, an expired certificate, or Flux rolling a tag whose
# migration failed against real data — it boots with its own environment. Equally
# this can never gate a release: by the time it is red, users are already broken.
# It is a detector and an alarm, not a gate.
#
# READ-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION. `events` is append-only, so a smoke that writes
# cannot clean up after itself. Every request below is a GET or an
# unauthenticated POST that is expected to be REJECTED. Nothing is created.
#
# Usage: prod-smoke.sh [base-url]
# Env:
#   PROD_URL       base URL (default https://app.lobu.ai)
#   EXPECT_SHA     if set, require this commit to be an ancestor of the
#                  deployed revision — i.e. "the rollout actually landed"
#   ROLLOUT_WAIT   seconds to wait for EXPECT_SHA to appear (default 0 = no wait)

set -uo pipefail

BASE="${1:-${PROD_URL:-https://app.lobu.ai}}"
BASE="${BASE%/}"
EXPECT_SHA="${EXPECT_SHA:-}"
ROLLOUT_WAIT="${ROLLOUT_WAIT:-0}"
# ROLLOUT_WAIT feeds `[ ... -ge ... ]` in the rollout loop; a non-integer would
# make that test error forever and spin until the job timeout instead of failing.
case "$ROLLOUT_WAIT" in
  *[!0-9]*)
    echo "ROLLOUT_WAIT must be a non-negative integer (seconds), got: ${ROLLOUT_WAIT}" >&2
    exit 1

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **`events.id` is a stored-version id, not stable source identity.** Connector resyncs can supersede a row and allocate a new id for the same source item. Cross-sync identity and dedupe must use the connector's stable `origin_id` (scoped to its connection/source) or an explicit domain key, never `events.id`.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Mutation checks require proof that the mutation landed: assert the old pattern exists, verify a countable source change, and confirm the focused test fails before restoring the fix and rerunning green. A green test after a no-op mutation proves nothing.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- **Agents never approve their own UI proof.** For an Owletto pointer PR, `make ui-review` posts the exact approval command on the Owletto PR; only a human admin may post that command. The agent must open the linked PR, stop before merge, and rerun the gate after the human comment. A changed pointer or proof invalidates the approval.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. `make ui-review`. It passes non-Owletto changes as not applicable. For an Owletto pointer change, first run `ARTIFACT=<hosted-html-url> OPEN=1 make ui-review`; it posts the proof on the exact merged Owletto PR, opens that PR for the human, and leaves the required `ui-review` status pending. Stop. After the human posts the displayed `/ui-approve <sha>` comment, rerun `make ui-review` and require success.
10. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
11. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Never introduce a new table or change the database design, API surface, or SDK surface without explicitly surfacing the proposal and receiving user confirmation first.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and pass that URL as `ARTIFACT` to `make ui-review`. The gate records it on the Owletto PR and binds human approval to the exact parent-base and Owletto-pointer pair.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Mutation checks require proof that the mutation landed: assert the old pattern exists, verify a countable source change, and confirm the focused test fails before restoring the fix and rerunning green. A green test after a no-op mutation proves nothing.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- **Agents never approve their own UI proof.** For an Owletto pointer PR, `make ui-review` posts the exact approval command on the Owletto PR; only a human admin may post that command. The agent must open the linked PR, stop before merge, and rerun the gate after the human comment. A changed pointer or proof invalidates the approval.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. `make ui-review`. It passes non-Owletto changes as not applicable. For an Owletto pointer change, first run `ARTIFACT=<hosted-html-url> OPEN=1 make ui-review`; it posts the proof on the exact merged Owletto PR, opens that PR for the human, and leaves the required `ui-review` status pending. Stop. After the human posts the displayed `/ui-approve <sha>` comment, rerun `make ui-review` and require success.
10. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
11. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Never introduce a new table or change the database design, API surface, or SDK surface without explicitly surfacing the proposal and receiving user confirmation first.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and pass that URL as `ARTIFACT` to `make ui-review`. The gate records it on the Owletto PR and binds human approval to the exact parent-base and Owletto-pointer pair.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

## 1. No — `feat/behavior-executors` was not shipped in this context

It was already shipped **before this session started**. PR #2499 squash-merged at 12:08 UTC today as `317323f70`; the branch's newest commit is 11:41 UTC, so nothing on it postdates the merge.

The reason it *looks* unshipped is the documented squash-ancestry trap — `git log origin/main..HEAD` reports 14 commits because a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link. Checked by content instead:

```
git diff origin/main 39d40049f -- <files from the newest commit>
(empty — identical)
```

I never touched the main checkout. All my work was in `.claude/worktrees/`. The `M .claude/settings.json`, `.env.example`, `.gitignore`, `config/providers.json`, `model-resolver.ts` edits that were dirty at session start got committed by something else mid-session — #2523 (yours, 17:23) is the `.gitignore` one.

One open item on that branch from memory, unrelated to me: the **dual-executor regression** — device-first silently steals agent rows, and the write path still allows two executors. Root defect, unfixed.

## 2. Failover — and I agree, no hacky stuff

Here's the thing: the non-hacky version is now *smaller* than it was this morning, because #2525 supplied the missing piece.

**What's actually broken.** One provider going dry takes a workspace to zero. Switching the org default (z-ai → gemini → z-ai over Jul 31) doesn't add resilience, it just moves which vendor is the single point of failure.

**The design.** Don't add runtime retry-and-reroute. There is already a pre-dispatch walk over candidate models — `provider-catalog.ts` iterates `agents.settings.models` checking each for credential presence and routability. It just doesn't check *health*. So:

> Make `providerIsRoutable()` consult `inference_providers.status`. A provider marked `error` is skipped, and the existing walk picks the next candidate on its own.

That's the whole change. No second retry budget, no mid-turn reroute, no new lock, no new table. Failover becomes a *consequence* of health plus the allow-list that already exists, which is exactly what the "coordination design brake" invariant asks for. It's fail-open by construction: if every candidate is marked unhealthy, you get today's behavior (try anyway) rather than a refusal to run.

Note I deliberately did **not** wire this in #2525 — `status` is observational there on purpose, and I said so in the PR. Making it a routing input is the separate, deliberate step.

**The hacky versions I'd refuse:** mid-turn retry-and-reroute in the worker (second retry budget, double token spend, half-streamed replies); blind retry in the secret-proxy (no classification at that layer); a per-org in-memory cooldown map (breaks multi-replica).

**What actually blocks it — and only one of these is engineering:**

The real blocker is that **there is usually nothing to fail over to.** `agents.settings.models` is an allow-list, and in practice it holds one entry — buremba's `personal-agent` was literally `["z-ai/glm-5.2"]`. Health-aware routing over a one-element list is a no-op. So failover isn't blocked on cleverness, it's blocked on users declaring a second choice, which is a product/UX question about how a "backup provider" gets surfaced.

The two genuine decisions for you:

- **Whose money.** If a customer's key runs dry and we fall back to a Lobu-funded provider, Lobu pays for their inference.
- **Vendor consent.** Silently routing a workspace's prompts to a vendor they didn't configure may be unacceptable on data-residency grounds.

If the answer to both is "only fail over between providers the customer configured and funded themselves," then this is small and I can build it: health-aware routability plus surfacing an ordered provider list in the agent config. If Lobu-funded fallback is on the table, that's a billing design first.

## Status of the rest

#2521 merged and prod-verified. #2525 merged, rollout gate running. #2526 (biome) CI running. I'll report when both land. The owed verification I flagged still stands: after #2525 deploys, exhaust a provider and confirm the row flips to `error`, then that a good turn clears it — that seam has no test.

content.text:
I pulled the actual code path and your live config so this is concrete rather than abstract.

## The walk has two modes, and the decisions only bite in one

`provider-catalog.ts:394` branches on whether the agent has a `settings.models` allow-list:

| | candidates the walk considers |
|---|---|
| **Restricted** (`settings.models` non-empty) | exactly the listed refs — *"NO org-default safety tail"*, no system-key tail |
| **Allow-all** (empty/absent) | org default → other org rows → **every `module.hasSystemKey()` deployment module** |

That last tier is Lobu's own keys. It already exists in the code today — it just only fires when a credential is *absent*, never when one 429s.

So "health-aware routing" means two very different things depending on the mode, and that's the part I don't think I made clear.

**In restricted mode, skipping an unhealthy provider can only ever move between providers the customer listed and pays for.** The walk structurally cannot reach Lobu's keys. There is no money question and no vendor question. It's pure engineering and I can build it without asking you anything.

**In allow-all mode, skipping walks down into `hasSystemKey()` modules** — Lobu's keys, at Lobu's expense, at a different vendor. That's where both decisions live.

## So the two decisions, stated properly

**1. Whose money.** In allow-all mode only: when we skip a customer's dry provider, may the walk keep going into the deployment/system-key tier? Yes means Lobu's key silently serves that customer's traffic — no cap, no notification, you find out on the invoice. No means we stop at the org's own rows.

**2. Vendor consent.** Same branch, different axis: those system-key modules are *other vendors*. A customer who configured Gemini and got quietly served by OpenAI has had their prompts sent to a company they never chose. Fine for a hobby workspace, not fine for anyone with a data-processing agreement.

Both are the same code line. Answering "no" to either kills that tier and leaves restricted-mode failover untouched.

## Why none of it helps you today

Your live config:

```
providers:  gemini (default, active) · openai (active — but "no credits remaining")
personal-agent.settings.models: ["gemini/gemini-2.5-pro"]
```

That's restricted mode with **one entry**. If Gemini 429s, the walk has exactly one candidate, fails closed, and every Behavior dies — and health-aware skipping changes nothing, because there is nothing to skip *to*. Your only other configured provider is also out of money.

This is what I meant by "failover isn't blocked on code." With one funded provider, no routing logic produces failover.

## What I'd actually do

1. **Health-aware skip in restricted mode.** Small, safe, needs no decision from you. Inert until step 2.
2. **Surface a backup provider** so the list can hold more than one entry. This is the step that makes failover real, and it's a UX question, not a billing one.
3. **Defer the allow-all/system-key tier entirely** until someone actually asks for Lobu-funded fallback. It's a billing feature wearing routing clothes.

One sub-decision I'd just make myself rather than escalate: if *every* candidate is marked `error`, try anyway rather than refuse. Health is an observational label and can be stale — the provider may have been topped up a minute ago, and a stale label should never be the thing that stops a workspace running.

Tell me if (1)+(2) is the shape you want and I'll scope it. Meanwhile #2521 is prod-verified, #2525 merged with its rollout gate running, #2526 in CI.

content.text:
You're right, and I should withdraw that recommendation rather than defend it.

## Why it's unreliable, concretely

**Behaviors are tuned to a model, not to "an LLM."** The 367-failure class in this same incident was `Agent reply finished without calling run_sdk (completeWindow)` — a tool-calling failure. Tool-calling reliability is one of the sharpest differences between models. Silently moving a Behavior from `gemini-2.5-pro` to `gpt-4o-mini` doesn't preserve it working; it swaps one failure mode for another, and the new one *looks like success* until you read the output.

**The run record can't even tell you it happened.** I checked: `runs` has `model_used` and `run_metadata`, and there is **no provider column**. `model_used` is currently stamped `'lobu-agent'` for platform runs. So after a silent swap you'd have a green run, different output, and nothing on the row saying a different vendor served it. That is exactly the trap that already cost a debugging session here — `model_used` looked like an observation and was a default. I'd be rebuilding that trap deliberately.

**It makes Behaviors non-reproducible.** Same Behavior, same input, different output depending on which provider happened to be healthy at dispatch. Anything comparing runs across time — `skip_if_unchanged`, classifiers, embeddings — gets unstable input.

**And it's driven off a stale label.** `inference_providers.status` is observational by design. Routing on it means model choice becomes a function of background state you can't see or predict.

## What I think the actual gap is

Reading #2350 again with that in mind: the problem was never "no failover." It was **nobody was told for two days.** Failover is a workaround for not being told.

#2521 and #2525 already fixed the two halves of that — stop burning runs, and record *why* on the provider row. What's still missing is the last hop: **nothing notifies you when a provider flips to `error`.** #2525 wrote the signal and left it sitting in a table you have to go look at.

That's the piece I'd build instead. It's smaller than failover, it needs no product decision, and it preserves determinism: you get told within a cron tick that z-ai is out of credit, and *you* decide whether to top up or switch models. A deliberate switch you made is reliable in a way an automatic one never is.

## Where that leaves failover

Not "never" — but not implicit, and not as the answer to this incident. If it's ever wanted it needs three things this design didn't have:

- the user declares the fallback explicitly per Behavior or per agent, so the swap is a configured choice rather than an inferred one;
- the run row records which provider actually served it, so a swapped run is visible in the history, not silent;
- the swap is surfaced on the run, not just permitted.

That's a real feature with a real cost. It is not a quota fix.

So: I'd drop items (1) and (2) from what I proposed last message, and replace them with alerting on the health signal. Want me to scope that?

content.text:
## What "system keys" are

Deployment-wide env vars on the **server pod** — one per provider, declared in `config/providers.json` as `envVarName`:

```
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY  OPENAI_API_KEY  GEMINI_API_KEY  Z_AI_API_KEY
OPENROUTER_API_KEY  GROQ_API_KEY  MISTRAL_API_KEY  DEEPSEEK_API_KEY  …
```

`hasSystemKey()` is literally `!!resolveEnv(envVar)` — "is that variable set on this deployment." It's the last tier of the credential chain: per-user auth profile → org's `inference_providers` row → **deployment env**.

So a system key is *your* key, not the customer's. In your local `.env` five are set (OPENROUTER, Z_AI, ANTHROPIC, OPENAI, GEMINI); in prod it's whatever the sealed-secret carries. That's the entire reason I flagged "whose money" — that tier is Lobu's account, and it sits at the end of the allow-all walk today.

## And yes — your instinct is right, and it's simpler than what I described

The admin surface **already exists and is already ordered**. `agents.settings.models` is an ordered array, and it's already both the allow-list gate *and* the selector. Yours is:

```
personal-agent.settings.models = ["gemini/gemini-2.5-pro"]
```

Today only position `[0]` effectively routes. Positions 1..n are used purely as a permission list — never as fallbacks. So the list already *looks* like a preference order and doesn't behave like one.

The change is to make it mean what it looks like:

```
["gemini/gemini-2.5-pro", "openai/gpt-4.1"]
   ↑ normal                  ↑ used only when gemini is marked error
```

Admin-declared, explicit, ordered, per-agent. And critically — **this never touches the system-key tier**. That tier is only reachable in allow-all mode; a non-empty list is exactly the listed refs with no tail. So configuring fallback this way makes both product decisions disappear: every candidate is a provider the customer put in their own org and pays for themselves.

That's a much better answer than mine. I was treating failover as a routing feature; you're treating it as configuration, which is what makes it predictable.

## The one thing it still needs

Your earlier objection doesn't fully go away. Declaring the order makes the swap *authorized*, but not *visible* — at 3am a Behavior would quietly run on gpt-4.1 and you'd have no way to tell from the run. `runs` has no provider column, and `model_used` is stamped `'lobu-agent'` for platform runs.

So I'd make it a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have: **a run that used a fallback records which provider and model served it, and says so on the run.** Otherwise we're back to a green run whose output silently came from somewhere else.

With that, the shape is:
1. Ordered `settings.models` becomes a real preference order, skipping providers marked `error`.
2. The run records the serving provider/model.
3. Notify when a provider flips to `error`, so you top up rather than living on the fallback indefinitely.

(3) matters because otherwise a workspace silently runs on its second choice forever and nobody notices the first one is dead — which is the original bug wearing a different hat.

Want me to scope that as a PR? It needs no product decision now that the system-key tier is out of scope.

**Status:** #2521 merged and prod-verified. #2525 merged, rollout gate still running. #2526 had a transient `check-drift` failure (8s, same owletto pin that passed twice today) — re-run requested.

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

<!-- Project rules for agents (Claude, pi, codex). CLAUDE.md inlines this into every session — keep this file lean. Put package-specific detail in the nearest package AGENTS.md. -->

## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **`events.id` is a stored-version id, not stable source identity.** Connector resyncs can supersede a row and allocate a new id for the same source item. Cross-sync identity and dedupe must use the connector's stable `origin_id` (scoped to its connection/source) or an explicit domain key, never `events.id`.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Mutation checks require proof that the mutation landed: assert the old pattern exists, verify a countable source change, and confirm the focused test fails before restoring the fix and rerunning green. A green test after a no-op mutation proves nothing.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- **Agents never approve their own UI proof.** For an Owletto pointer PR, `make ui-review` posts the exact approval command on the Owletto PR; only a human admin may post that command. The agent must open the linked PR, stop before merge, and rerun the gate after the human comment. A changed pointer or proof invalidates the approval.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. `make ui-review`. It passes non-Owletto changes as not applicable. For an Owletto pointer change, first run `ARTIFACT=<hosted-html-url> OPEN=1 make ui-review`; it posts the proof on the exact merged Owletto PR, opens that PR for the human, and leaves the required `ui-review` status pending. Stop. After the human posts the displayed `/ui-approve <sha>` comment, rerun `make ui-review` and require success.
10. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
11. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Never introduce a new table or change the database design, API surface, or SDK surface without explicitly surfacing the proposal and receiving user confirmation first.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and pass that URL as `ARTIFACT` to `make ui-review`. The gate records it on the Owletto PR and binds human approval to the exact parent-base and Owletto-pointer pair.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

---
name: reference_check_drift_is_gated_by_ui_approve
description: "When owletto/main's tip contains an un-UI-approved change, check-drift on every lobu PR cannot be fixed by a bump PR — the pending /ui-approve IS the drift fix, and bumping separately would route around the gate"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 5b3a8fb5-1a3b-47a3-a6e5-aa4b52e14cb0
  modified: 2026-08-05T14:16:08.912Z
---

`check-drift` fails on **every open lobu PR** whenever `owletto/main` has commits past the pinned
submodule SHA:

```
owletto/main has merged commits past the pinned SHA. The parent bump PR is missing.
Pinned:       <sha>
owletto/main: <sha>
Fix (open as a separate PR): ... git commit -m 'chore(submodule): bump owletto to current main'
```

**Do NOT blindly follow that suggested fix.** If `owletto/main`'s tip contains a UI change whose
lobu-side pointer PR is still waiting on `/ui-approve`, opening a separate bump PR to that tip would
**ship the unapproved UI to prod** — routing around the `ui-review` gate rather than satisfying it.
In that situation the pending human approval IS the drift fix. Stop and say so; don't "unblock" it.

There is no partial escape either: pinning an *earlier* ancestor (e.g. only the infra commits) leaves
the UI commit still past the pin, so check-drift keeps failing. The pointer must reach the tip.

Seen 2026-08-05: my own owletto k8s merges (#725–#731) pushed `owletto/main` ahead and broke
check-drift on 4 lobu PRs at once. Three pointer PRs were open simultaneously, each pinning a
different point in owletto history and each needing its OWN ui-review approval — merge order matters
and only the last one reaches the tip:

| lobu PR | pins | note |
|---|---|---|
| #2508 | `ef0ffc1e` | oldest |
| #2509 | `776eb120` | |
| #2511 | `400bcb14` | = owletto/main tip, the one that actually clears drift |

**Diagnostic reflex:** a PR failing only `check-drift` almost never has a problem of its own. Confirm
with `gh api /repos/lobu-ai/lobu/pulls/<n>/files --jq '.[] | select(.filename=="packages/owletto") | .patch'`
to read what each pointer PR pins (`gh pr diff | grep Subproject` does NOT work — the submodule hunk
is not in the text diff), and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> <tip>` to order them. Don't spend a
CI cycle "fixing" the PR itself.

Related: [[reference_worktree_stale_submodule_pin_fails_check_drift]], [[reference_submodule_merge_order]],

======
---
name: feedback_merge_owletto_pr_last_not_first
description: Merging the Owletto PR before its parent pointer PR turns check-drift red on EVERY open lobu PR — hold the submodule merge until the parent is ready to land
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: f4e4deab-cb97-4427-8120-e77084d6508a
  modified: 2026-08-05T14:33:24.360Z
---

Merging an Owletto PR advances `owletto/main` past the SHA that `lobu/main`
pins. `check-drift` then fails on **every open lobu PR in the repo**, not just
the one carrying the bump — it compares the pinned SHA against `owletto/main`
and cannot pass until a pointer bump lands on `lobu/main`.

Done 2026-08-05 (owletto#723 merged while its parent lobu#2509 was still
waiting on a human `/ui-approve`): six open PRs went red on a check none of
their authors could fix.

**Why:** check-drift's own rule says the pinned SHA must be reachable from
`owletto/main`, which reads like "merge owletto first". It is the opposite. The
pointer PR carries the bump, so the safe order is:

1. Get the parent lobu PR fully green **including `ui-review` approval**.
2. Merge the Owletto PR.
3. Repin to the merged SHA, push, let check-drift go green.
4. Merge the parent.

Holding the Owletto PR open scopes the red to your own PR (pinned SHA not
reachable) instead of blocking everyone.

**How to apply:** before `gh pr merge` on an owletto PR, check whether the
parent lobu PR can merge in the same sitting. If it is blocked on a human gate,
leave the submodule PR open.

Related: [[reference_submodule_merge_order]],
[[reference_worktree_stale_submodule_pin_fails_check_drift]]

description: Prod DB cluster is now lobu-ai-prod-db (replaced summaries-db) after the 2026-05-20 test-against-prod wipe + PITR recovery
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 023a3362-eb2f-4af1-958e-fb1aa8a9d18d
  modified: 2026-07-29T23:53:01.706Z
---

On 2026-05-20 the `summaries-prod` production `owletto` database (49 orgs / 36 users / ~1.17M events, ~12GB) was **wiped**: a developer ran the integration test suite locally with `DATABASE_URL` pointed at prod; `__tests__/setup/test-db.ts` setup runs `DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE` and the `summaries` role owns the DB, so it succeeded (ran ~16:59–17:27 UTC). NOT CI (CI uses throwaway `lobu_test`).

**Recovery:** CNPG PITR from R2 backup lineage `summaries-db-v2` to 2026-05-20 16:00 UTC (latest verified-complete snapshot) into a NEW cluster **`lobu-ai-prod-db`** (clean name chosen by user). The old `summaries-db` was retired/deleted.

**Current prod topology (CNPG on k8s, ns `summaries-prod`):**
- DB cluster `lobu-ai-prod-db` + pooler `lobu-ai-prod-db-pooler` + daily ScheduledBackup; backups to R2 serverName `lobu-ai-prod-db`.
- GitOps-managed at `packages/owletto/deploy/k8s/apps/lobu-db/` via its OWN Flux Kustomization `lobu-db` (separate path so it escapes the lobu app overlay's `summaries-` namePrefix → keeps the clean name). The lobu app overlay (`apps/lobu/overlays/summaries-prod`) no longer defines a DB; app+migrate `poolerService` point at `lobu-ai-prod-db-pooler` / `lobu-ai-prod-db-rw`.
- App DB creds secret `summaries-db-app` (NOT cluster-owned — survives cluster deletion). R2 creds `summaries-r2-backup-credentials` (SealedSecret).

**Prevention shipped (lobu#989, merged `df38fbf4`):** `getTestDb()` refuses any DB whose name isn't test-shaped (`assertSafeTestDatabaseUrl`; override `LOBU_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_TEST_DB=1`); baseline `00000000000000_baseline.sql` `migrate:down` is now `RAISE EXCEPTION` (was `DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE`). owletto #208 (cutover) + #209 (GitOps codify) merged.

**Querying prod (verified 2026-07-30).** The database is named **`owletto`** — not `lobu`, not `app`. `app` exists and is empty of app tables, so a wrong `-d` fails with a confusing `relation "runs" does not exist` rather than a missing-database error. The primary pod has two containers, so `-c postgres` is required:

```
kubectl exec -n summaries-prod lobu-ai-prod-db-1 -c postgres -- \
  psql -U postgres -d owletto -A -F$'\t' -c "<sql>"
```

Column names that do not exist and cost a retry each: `runs.updated_at` / `runs.approved_at` (the real ones are `created_at, completed_at, claimed_at, last_heartbeat_at, run_at, expires_at`), `entities.merged_into_id` (it is `merged_into`), `entity_identities.kind` (it is `namespace`). There is no `notifications` table.

**PITR recovery runbook lessons (do these BEFORE cutover next time):** (1) PITR resets planner statistics → run `ANALYZE` or queries seq-scan and time out (`resolve_path` hit this). (2) A hand-made recovery cluster has NONE of the chart's tuning/resources — copy `shared_buffers`/`random_page_cost=1.1`/`effective_cache_size`/resources from the chart. (3) `geo_earthdistance` migration needs `cube`+`earthdistance` extensions pre-created as superuser (app role can't CREATE untrusted earthdistance) and conflicts with pre-squash `geo_lookup(p_lat,…)` (`DROP FUNCTION` it first). (4) CNPG `bootstrap` is immutable — a GitOps manifest adopting an existing recovered cluster MUST replicate its exact bootstrap or the webhook rejects the apply. (5) Flux `prune: true` on the apps Kustomization — removing a cluster from render deletes it; verify `kustomize build` before merge.

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific.
